title: Fail closed instead of degrading when a compiled Check lacks a capability
summary: The manifest that CompiledInteractiveController derives from a CompiledPluginContract set capability_missing_outcome to needs_review while its decision states were the five compiled terminal states (satisfied, violated, not_applicable, unknown, blocked). needs_review is not a compiled decision state, so this only worked because missing capabilities are normally rejected during provider binding; if the Kernel's missing-capability branch were ever reached it would have emitted a v1 result word on the compiled surface. This change sets capability_missing_outcome to blocked, the fail-closed outcome the plugin-manifest schema reserves for this case and the only value the Kernel turns into a CAPABILITY_MISSING work failure, and adds a test asserting the compiled manifest fails closed. No compiled contract, plugin case, schema, published artifact, or normal-path behaviour changes: the field is internal to the controller's manifest and the missing-capability branch stays unreachable on the normal path.

platform: Platform governance owns the compiled interactive manifest and its fail-closed capability outcome
plugin: No plugin change; compiled plugins keep declaring capabilities in their contract
provider: No provider change; capability binding still fails before this branch

forbiddenResponsibilities: The change must not add needs_review or any other v1 result word to the compiled decision states
The change must not alter the compiled Plugin Contract output or the normal provider-binding path
The change must not change the frozen v1 SDK decision vocabulary
acceptance: the compiled controller's manifest declares capability_missing_outcome blocked
blocked is one of the declared decision states and needs_review is not
the architecture, document, plugin-source, English text and resilience gates return 0 and the fast and full profiles stay green

humanApproval.decision: Internal-only alignment carried out under the standing authorization of the refactor mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19 and its delegation update, under which the agent and reviewer decide these changes themselves within at most seven workflow rounds. No compiled contract, schema, published artifact, or normal-path behaviour changes: the retired v1 word is replaced by the schema-reserved fail-closed outcome on an internal manifest field.
